name: LIS2MDL 3-axis magnetometer
description: STMicroelectronics 3-axis magnetometer (compass sensor) with a fixed ±49.152 gauss range, 1.5 mgauss/LSB 16-bit output, I2C or SPI. Chip runs on 1.71–3.6 V; the breakout has a 3.3 V regulator and level shifting for 3–5 V. Sold as: Adafruit LIS2MDL Triple-axis Magnetometer (#4488, STEMMA QT; 7-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, SDO, CS), fixed I2C address 0x1E.
eli5: Feels magnetic fields in three directions, so your project can tell which way is north or notice a nearby magnet.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3–5 V (on-board AP2112K 3.3 V regulator; use your board's logic voltage)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (SPI clock in SPI mode); level-shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (SPI data in 3-wire SPI mode); level-shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: SDO
pins.description: Chip pin INT/DRDY/SDO: interrupt or data-ready output (3.3 V push-pull once enabled), or SPI data out in 4-wire SPI; 10 kΩ pull-down on the board, not needed for basic use

pins.name: CS
pins.description: SPI chip select; pulled up to 3.3 V on the board so I2C is used, leave unconnected for I2C

buildNotes: For I2C you only need VIN, GND, SCL and SDA; leave CS unconnected (the board pulls it high, which selects I2C).

Reset default is idle (CFG_REG_A = 0x03): write CFG_REG_A (0x60) = 0x80 for temperature compensation, 10 Hz, high-resolution, continuous mode, or every reading stays the same. ST says COMP_TEMP_EN must be 1 for proper operation.
WHO_AM_I (0x4F) reads 0x40. The I2C address is fixed at 0x1E, so it clashes with an LSM303 / LIS3MDL at 0x1E on the same bus.
Read the six output bytes in one burst from register 0x68 | 0x80 (the top bit asks for auto-increment); values are 16-bit two's complement, low byte first.
Sensitivity is fixed at 1.5 mgauss per LSB (range ±49.152 gauss). Earth's field is about 0.25–0.65 gauss (25–65 µT).
The SDO pin is the chip's INT/DRDY output in I2C mode (set DRDY_on_PIN in CFG_REG_C to use it as data-ready).
Keep it away from motors, speakers, steel screws and wires carrying more than 10 mA, which swamp the Earth's field.

driver.code:
# LIS2MDL 3-axis magnetometer (STMicroelectronics), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the ST datasheet DocID030621 Rev 5: I2C address 0x1E (fixed), WHO_AM_I 0x4F = 0x40,
# CFG_REG_A/B/C at 0x60..0x62, STATUS_REG 0x67, OUTX_L..OUTZ_H at 0x68..0x6D
# (two's complement, LSB at the lower address), sensitivity 1.5 mgauss/LSB, range +/-49.152 gauss.
# In I2C the MSb of the register address asks for auto-increment, so a 6-byte burst starts at 0x68 | 0x80.
import time

_WHO_AM_I = 0x4F
_CFG_REG_A = 0x60
_CFG_REG_B = 0x61
_CFG_REG_C = 0x62
_STATUS_REG = 0x67
_OUTX_L = 0x68

_SENS_GAUSS = 0.0015  # 1.5 mgauss per LSB (datasheet Table 3)
_ODR = {10: 0x00, 20: 0x04, 50: 0x08, 100: 0x0C}  # ODR[1:0] in CFG_REG_A (Table 25)


class LIS2MDL:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x1E, odr_hz=10):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        who = self._r(_WHO_AM_I, 1)[0]
        if who != 0x40:
            raise OSError('LIS2MDL not found (WHO_AM_I=0x%02X): check wiring' % who)
        if odr_hz not in _ODR:
            raise ValueError('odr_hz must be 10, 20, 50 or 100')
        # CFG_REG_A: SOFT_RST (bit 5) resets the configuration and user registers
        self._w(_CFG_REG_A, 0x20)
        time.sleep_ms(20)
        # CFG_REG_C: BDU=1 (bit 4) so a reading's low and high bytes always belong together;
        # I2C_DIS=0, BLE=0 (LSB at lower address), 4WSPI=0
        self._w(_CFG_REG_C, 0x10)
        # CFG_REG_B: OFF_CANC=1 (bit 1) offset cancellation, LPF off
        self._w(_CFG_REG_B, 0x02)
        # CFG_REG_A: COMP_TEMP_EN=1 (must be 1 for proper operation), LP=0 high-resolution,
        # ODR, MD=00 continuous mode (reset default MD=11 is idle)
        self._w(_CFG_REG_A, 0x80 | _ODR[odr_hz])
        # turn-on time 9.4 ms + 1/ODR with offset cancellation (Table 12)
        time.sleep_ms(10 + 1000 // odr_hz + 10)

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def read_raw(self):
        """Raw signed counts (x, y, z)."""
        for _ in range(50):  # wait for Zyxda (bit 3), at most about 0.5 s
            if self._r(_STATUS_REG, 1)[0] & 0x08:
                break
            time.sleep_ms(10)
        d = self._r(_OUTX_L | 0x80, 6)
        out = []
        for i in (0, 2, 4):
            v = d[i] | (d[i + 1] << 8)
            out.append(v - 65536 if v & 0x8000 else v)
        return tuple(out)

    def read(self):
        """Magnetic field (x, y, z) in gauss (1 gauss = 100 uT)."""
        x, y, z = self.read_raw()
        return x * _SENS_GAUSS, y * _SENS_GAUSS, z * _SENS_GAUSS

    def read_ut(self):
        """Magnetic field (x, y, z) in microtesla."""
        return tuple(v * 100 for v in self.read())

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from lis2mdl import LIS2MDL

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
mag = LIS2MDL(i2c)
while True:
    x, y, z = mag.read()
    print('X=%.3f Y=%.3f Z=%.3f gauss' % (x, y, z))
    time.sleep(1)
